queries: WITH p AS (SELECT P.ID, P.SEX, AVG(L.ALB) AS alb, AVG(L.UN * 1.0 / NULLIF(L.`T-BIL`, 0)) AS ratio FROM Laboratory L JOIN Patient P ON P.ID = L.ID GROUP BY P.ID, P.SEX), s AS (SELECT SEX, AVG(alb) AS avg_alb, AVG(ratio) AS avg_ratio FROM p GROUP BY SEX), m AS (SELECT AVG(avg_alb) AS mean_alb FROM s) SELECT s.SEX, s.avg_alb, s.avg_ratio, s.avg_alb - m.mean_alb AS alb_above_mean FROM s CROSS JOIN m WHERE s.avg_alb > m.mean_alb

assumptions.assumption: A test with T-BIL = 0 has no computable ratio, so it is treated as NULL and ignored in the averages.
The 'mean of the sex-level ALB averages' is the unweighted average of the per-sex averages. Every sex group is included, and a NULL-sex group would count as its own group if one exists.

assumptions.assumption: A per-test ratio is UN divided by T-BIL, computed only where T-BIL is non-zero and both values are non-null. Zero T-BIL gives NULL, which AVG ignores.
The mean of the sex-level ALB averages is the unweighted average of the per-sex values. It is not weighted by patient or lab-record counts. Sexes whose average ALB is NULL are ignored.
Sex groups are taken as stored in Patient.SEX, so a NULL or blank SEX would form its own group.

responses.sql: WITH p AS (SELECT l.ID, p.SEX, AVG(l.ALB) AS alb, AVG(l.UN / NULLIF(l.`T-BIL`, 0)) AS ratio FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = l.ID GROUP BY l.ID, p.SEX), s AS (SELECT SEX, AVG(alb) AS avg_alb, AVG(ratio) AS avg_ratio FROM p GROUP BY SEX), m AS (SELECT AVG(avg_alb) AS mean_alb FROM s) SELECT s.SEX, s.avg_alb, s.avg_ratio, s.avg_alb - m.mean_alb AS alb_above_mean FROM s CROSS JOIN m WHERE s.avg_alb > m.mean_alb

assumptions.assumption: Rows with T-BIL = 0 have an incomputable ratio and are treated as NULL (ignored by AVG); NULL T-BIL or UN likewise.
The 'mean of the sex-level ALB averages' is the unweighted mean of the per-sex averages (one value per sex), not weighted by patient count or lab rows.
Sex groups are taken as they appear in Patient.SEX; a NULL/empty SEX, if present, forms its own group and counts in the mean, as would any other group with a non-null ALB average.
